decisions.reason: The cleaning-method decision does not change the separate leak-prevention requirements. The same source message's sealing clause is already represented by an independent candidate Event.

Making the spout removable or easy to flush does not change its valve mechanism, closed-valve behavior, or required flow behavior. Those independent clauses from the same message are already represented.
The cleaning requirement permits either a removable spout or one that is easy to flush, so it does not necessarily alter the spout's location, orientation, pouring goal, or selected design reference.
The spout cleaning method has no effect on the machine name or placard wording.
The requirement to remove or flush residue from the spout does not change the bowl's capacity or deep-well form.
Spout removability or flushability for cleaning does not change the splash-control target for mixing operation.
The sanitary spout decision does not affect the green accent color requirement.
The spout cleaning method does not change the DJ-turntable-inspired visual identity.
The cleaning constraint may inform downstream design work, but it does not change the current CAD deliverable or its adopted design direction.
